### Dedicated to the well-being of their customers

UnaliWear customer service is beyond excellent. The customer service I receive with my Kanega watch
is the result of a company culture that is dedicated to the well-being of their customers.

#### Dave L

### I've loved it since I put it on

My daughter-in-law found the Kanega watch for me. I’ve loved it since I put it on. I have Cerebral
Palsy, and I live alone. Falls have become more frequent in recent years. Now that I have the watch,
my kids are far less worried. I love keeping it on night and day, even in the shower.

#### Barb L

### A real human checks in

It works about anywhere with both wifi and cellular — and Verizon service is included. A real human
checks in as if by phone after a fall, a button press, or a voice command and false alarms are easy
to dismiss. The company will also increase/decrease the sensitivity of any band on request.

#### Erick H

### A great alternative to an Apple Watch

A great alternative to an Apple Watch designed specifically for seniors. I have been very pleased
with my watch so far. It is a reasonably priced way to ensure that someone left alone for many hours
in the day is still connected to the outside world to maintain his safety.

#### Jerry M

### Operated just like my cell phone

I unfortunately live in a dead cell zone on the coast and both my landline and cell signals are
degraded for various reasons. The Kanega watch was the only product I found that operated just like
my cell phone – using my WiFi signal and home and cell service when I am out and about.

#### Elizabeth P

### How can any one in 2023 not get this?

Did a lot of research including the Apple Watch which, while appealing, had a number of drawbacks
including the fact it connects directly to 911 not a service. Finally found the Kanega which had
distinct advantages.
1) Does not come off, just snap in the recharged batteries and snap the others in the charger.
2) Connects to a service not 911…
3) Waterproof. How can any one in 2023 not get this?

#### Michael S

### Nice looking, easy to use, reliable for fall detection

After an exhaustive search for exactly the right thing for us, and something he would wear, we were
happy to find the Kanega watch by UnaliWear… Nice looking, easy to use, reliable for fall detection,
and comfortable to wear! And the customer service is amazing.

#### Ann O

### Greater confidence in the product

My mother has had one fall since having the watch. The watch detected the fall. Fortunately she was
not seriously hurt and we didn’t have to get help but it brought her, and us greater confidence in
the product.

#### Kevin W

### I really love my Kanega Watch

I really love my Kanega Watch. I never have to take it off, which is really comforting, and I don’t
have to look like an old person with an alert device around my neck.

#### Richard S

### Life saviour

My 93 year old father wandered into the garage at 2:30 am. one night. The lights went out and he
fell. Thank goodness he was wearing his Kanega Watch. We immediately received a call that he had
fallen.

#### Linda J

### Ten stars

I had tried another Medical Alert device, but it only worked within my property line and was
expensive for what it did (or didn’t) do. I sent it back and spent the next several years looking
into other devices.

#### Carole H

### Best medical device

I looked for a long time for a medical device that was not a necklace. This Kanega Watch works great
and the best part is the staff. **************** is awesome, best I have seen anyway. They truly
care about your situation and your experience.

### Jean Anne Booth

##### CEO & Founder

A serial entrepreneur, Jean Anne started UnaliWear after selling previous startups to Texas
Instruments and Apple.
Jean Anne was the founder of Luminary Micro, the creators of the Stellaris microcontroller platform
and the first to market with ARM Cortex-M3-based microcontroller solutions. Luminary Micro was
purchased by Texas Instruments in May 2009, and was one of the top VC-backed M&As of 2009. Jean Anne
retired from TI in 2012 after serving as the general manager for TI’s Stellaris family of products.
Jean Anne was also a founder at Intrinsity, the creators of the graphics chip in Apple iPad
products. Intrinsity sold to Apple in 2010.
Jean Anne holds a BSEE from the University of Texas at Austin, and an MSCE from National Technical
University.

### Brian Kircher

Brian Kircher has over 25 years of experience creating comprehensive software platforms and

Stellaris microcontroller platform. After Texas Instruments acquired Luminary Micro in 2009, Brian
shared with TI’s microcontroller and microprocessor teams the StellarisWare philosophy of enabling
customer success through easy-to-use software. Earlier in his career, Brian worked at Cirrus Logic
and IBM.
Brian holds a BS in mathematics and computer science from Carnegie Mellon University.

## The Best Home Care for Your Senior Loved One That Supports Aging in Place

If you're looking for [professional in-home care][39] for an aging loved one, look no further than
Visiting Angels—an esteemed name families have relied on since 1998. As "America’s Choice in Home
Care," we’re proud to support the very best of home care—delivering compassionate, dependable
services to thousands of families nationwide.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Senior Home Care

What Services Do Visiting Angels Provide?

Visiting Angels offers non-medical [home care services][59] tailored to help seniors age safely and
comfortably at home. Our core services include, but are not limited to:
* **[Companion Care][60]:** Help with meal preparation, light housekeeping, and errands
* **[Personal Care:][61]** Assistance with bathing, dressing, grooming, and toileting
* **Specialized Care:** Dedicated support for Alzheimer’s, Dementia, palliative care, and
  end-of-life care
* **[Transition to Home Care][62]:** Helping seniors safely return home after a surgery or hospital
  stay
* **[Respite Care][63]:** Temporary relief for family caregivers

We offer flexible scheduling, from a few hours per week up to 24-hour or live-in care.

What Is the Difference Between Non-Medical Home Care and Home Health Care?

While “non-medical home care” and “home health care” sound similar, they are actually two distinct
services that are commonly confused. The main difference is the type of support provided and the
medical necessity behind it.

Home health care is clinical in nature, typically prescribed by a physician to treat a specific
medical condition or to help a patient recover from surgery, through services such as wound care and
physical therapy.

In contrast, non-medical home care—like the services provided by Visiting Angels—focuses on
assisting seniors with essential activities of daily living, such as meal preparation, mobility
assistance, and personal care, and more. Our devoted caregivers provide the consistent and
compassionate support seniors need to live safely and independently in their own homes.

How Much Does In-Home Care Cost?

The [cost of in-home care][64] varies and is tailored to your specific situation. Key factors that
influence professional home care costs include the level of care needed, frequency and duration of
visits, geographical location, and type of support required.

With Visiting Angels, you pay only for the help you actually need—whether a few hours a week or
[full-time home care support][65]—giving you a more affordable, flexible alternative to an assisted
living facility.

We also provide a free in-home consultation to assess your needs and provide a customized quote
tailored to your budget and care requirements.

How Do I Get Started With a Free Home Care Consultation?

Our free, no-obligation [in-home care consultation][66] provides expert guidance and answers your
care questions, helping you navigate the decision-making process with peace of mind and zero
pressure. An in-home consultation is a way for us to get to know your family and understand your
specific needs to create a care plan that feels right for your loved one.

[Get started with in-home care][67] by contacting your Visiting Angels [local home care agency][68]
to schedule a consultation at your loved one’s home.

If you’re a [long-distance caregiver][69], we will conduct a one-on-one in-home consultation with
your loved one and a detailed phone consultation with you.

Does Medicare or Insurance Cover In-Home Care Services?

Typically, Medicare and standard health insurance do not cover non-medical assistance with
activities of daily living that Visiting Angels primarily provides. However, you may find coverage
through the following:
* **Long-Term Care Insurance:** The most common form of private coverage for home care
* [**Veterans Benefits**][70]**:** Programs like Aid and Attendance can often be used for these
  services
* **Medicare Advantage (Part C):** Some private plans offer limited supplemental home care benefits
* **Medicaid:** May cover costs for those who meet specific financial and medical eligibility
  requirements

Because every policy is different, we recommend a [free consultation][71] to help you identify which
benefits apply to your situation.

How Quickly Can Home Care Services Start?

We understand that needs and situations can change quickly, so we strive to begin care as soon as
possible. While each Visiting Angels location is different, caregivers can typically start providing
services within 48 hours of your initial consultation. In some urgent situations, we may be able to
coordinate same-day support to ensure your loved one has the care they need right away.

Do You Provide Care in Assisted Living Facilities or Nursing Homes?

Yes, while Visiting Angels primarily serves seniors in their own homes, we can provide [supplemental
care to seniors residing in nursing homes][72] or assisted living facilities. Often, facility staff
members are stretched thin across many residents, and our presence can help your loved one receive
the dedicated, continuous attention they deserve.

Whether they need extra assistance with mobility, specialized memory support, or simply the comfort
of a consistent companion, we work alongside the facility's team to enhance your loved one's quality
of life.

## Affordable At-Home Protection Using Your Landline

The **Home Link** is Vital Link’s most affordable medical alert system, designed for Bay Area
seniors who still have an active landline telephone. This landline medical alert system connects
through your existing phone line with no special wiring, no internet, and no monthly equipment fees.
Press your wearable help button from anywhere in or around your home, and you are connected to our
24/7 monitoring center in seconds.

A local Vital Link technician will come to your home in Oakland, San Francisco, San Jose, or

2. **Speak directly** with a trained emergency operator through the base station’s two-way speaker.
3. **Help is dispatched** based on your personalized Emergency Care Plan, including calls to your
family, neighbors, or emergency services.

If you cannot respond after pressing the button, our operators follow your care plan automatically.
They will call your home, then dispatch help and begin contacting your emergency contacts.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What happens if I press the button but cannot speak?

Our operators will try to reach you by phone. If they cannot make contact, they immediately dispatch
emergency services and begin calling your emergency contacts based on your personalized care plan.

### Will the system work during a power outage?

Yes. The Home Link has an 80-hour backup battery. It also sends a low-battery signal to our
monitoring center so we can alert you proactively.

### Will this affect my phone service?

No. The Home Link has no effect on your regular phone service. It only uses the line briefly to dial
during emergencies and testing. These calls are toll-free, so you will not be charged.

### Can two people use the same system?

Yes. A second person in the same household can use the system with an additional wearable button
(one-time $40 fee). There is no extra monthly monitoring charge.

### Is the help button waterproof?

Yes. The wearable button is fully waterproof and should be worn in the bath or shower, where falls
are most common.

### What if my button breaks or the battery dies?

All equipment is covered by a lifetime replacement warranty. We replace buttons and ship batteries
at no cost to you. The button battery typically lasts 8 to 10 years.

### How large is the help button?

The pendant is a little bigger than a quarter and weighs about an ounce. It can be worn as a
necklace, on the wrist, or clipped to your clothing.

### What if I press the button by mistake?

Just tell the operator it was an accident and that you are fine. There is no penalty for accidental
presses.

### Can I take the system with me if I move?

Yes. The Home Link is portable. If you relocate within our Bay Area service area, we will reinstall
it at your new home, If you move out of the area your system will work but you will need to
reconnect it at the new location yourself.

counties. If your loved one is transitioning home after a hospital stay, we coordinate directly with

All equipment is covered by a lifetime replacement warranty at no extra cost. We also ship
replacement charging cradles for free. If something breaks, we fix it.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does fall detection work?

The Mobile W uses built-in sensors to detect major falls such as forward falls, backward falls, or
collapsing to the ground. If a fall is detected, the device automatically contacts our monitoring
center. You do not need to press the button.

### What if the device detects a fall that did not happen?

If the device triggers a false alert, simply tell the operator you are fine or cancel the alert on
the device. There is no penalty.

### How do I initiate a call manually?

Hold the button for just 1 second to start a call to our monitoring center.

### How often do I need to charge it?

The battery lasts 3 to 5 days depending on usage. Place the device face-up in the charging cradle. A
red light flashes while charging and turns solid when fully charged. The device will also give a
voice prompt confirming it is charging.

### Can I wear it in the shower?

Yes. The Mobile W is IP67 rated, making it safe for showers and outdoor use. It should not be fully
submerged in water such as in a bath or pool.

### Can I wear it differently than on my wrist?

Yes. The Mobile W comes with a wristband, but it is also compatible with an optional lanyard or belt
clip. The device uses standard 24mm quick-release bands, so you can swap in any compatible watch
band.

### Does the Mobile W work outside the Bay Area?

Yes. The device works anywhere in the United States with Verizon 4G LTE coverage. Many clients take
it when traveling or visiting family in other states.

### What happens if I press the button but cannot speak?

Our operators use GPS, Wi-Fi, and cellular triangulation to locate you and follow your Emergency
Care Plan automatically. They dispatch help and begin calling your emergency contacts.

### Do I need a phone line or internet?

No. The Mobile W uses its own built-in LTE cellular connection. It does not require a landline,
internet, or Wi-Fi.

### What if the device breaks?

All equipment is covered by a lifetime replacement warranty at no cost to you.

Our vision is to set the standard for compassionate care in the medical alert industry by treating

### Letter from CEO

It wasn’t long after I started Vital Link Medical Alert Systems back in 1981 that I began to
understand how we made a difference in people’s lives and how working with our clients began to
affect mine.

Back then, I assembled the equipment, handled the sales, installations, administration and made sure
that all our clients were comfortable with using Vital Link.

In the early days I was notified by our monitoring center on every emergency. Many times I would
receive multiple calls throughout the night to make sure that everything went as planned. As we
grew, I couldn’t do that for everyone, but I wanted to keep that personal touch alive. We are still
one of the few medical alert companies that does in home installations and checks up on our clients
to see how they’re after they have used our service.

#### [Read More][71]

Since I took part in all aspects of our business from the start, I’ve always felt very connected to
our clients and felt quite strongly how important Vital Link was to helping them keep their
independence while providing peace of mind to them and their families.

Since 1981, I’ve listened and learned from our clients’ stories and the reasons why they needed our
service. Many have told me how they had fallen and weren’t able to get help as they laid on the
floor all night. My heart went out to them, and I was honored to be able to present a solution to
keep them living safely and independently in their homes.

I always wanted to create a business that took care of people and focused on service and making a
positive impact on our community rather than concentrating on growth and profits. We have always
made a priority of supporting compassionate causes rather than spending resources on marketing and
advertising. We reduce our rates for low income clients, Meals on Wheels recipients and veterans as
a way to give back to those in need. Being President of the Board for Meals on Wheels of Alameda
County allowed me to serve many of our frail, homebound seniors on a volunteer basis. I started
providing pro bono service for our local Holocaust survivors after some of them shared their stories
with my son’s middle school class. I wanted to show him the importance of giving back to our
community and for him to hear the survivor’s experiences while we brought our systems into their
homes.

As a true family business, it’s very rewarding being able to work side by side with my son Asher who
grew up in our business and is now our Director of Operations. Over the years my wife, daughter,
sister, niece and close friends have been and are involved in our company.

In the early days I was able to provide Vital Link services and protect my grandparents and their
peers, then my parents and their friends and now my contemporaries. Even I relied on our service
when both of my hips were replaced and I had limited mobility.

Our goal is to make the entire process courteous, professional and seamless for our clients and
their families. We are here to provide solutions while communicating in a warm and personal way.
When you call us, you will always speak to one of our caring staff directly. There’s no pushing one
for this department or two for that department. Openness, honesty, integrity and respect are at our
core.

You can always be assured that we are going to treat you and yours like family and do exactly what
we say we are going to do. We work hard to go beyond and exceed our client’s expectations. We’re
here to make your life easier and provide you with security and peace of mind.

On behalf of our hardworking staff, I’d like to thank you for the trust you have placed in Vital
Link Medical Alert Systems.

Sincerely,

Arthur Hoffman,

CEO and Founder

# Mobile X: GPS Medical Alert with Fall Detection for Bay Area Seniors

Built-in fall detection, GPS tracking, two-way voice, and optional caregiver app. Starting at
$40.95/mo.

[Mobile X GPS medical alert with fall detection device held in hand]

## Automatic Fall Detection That Travels with You

The **Mobile X** is a GPS medical alert with fall detection built directly into the device. If it
senses a heavy fall, it automatically contacts our monitoring center, even if you are unable to
press the button yourself. Whether you are at home in Oakland, visiting friends in San Jose, or
traveling anywhere in the United States, this device keeps you protected around the clock.

For Bay Area seniors and their families, the Mobile X offers something most at-home systems cannot:
portable fall detection combined with real-time GPS tracking. If you or a loved one has experienced
a fall before, or if falling is a concern, this GPS medical alert with fall detection provides an
extra layer of safety that does not depend on being near a base station.

## How the Mobile X Works
1. **A fall is detected automatically** by sensors built into the device, or you press the help
button manually from anywhere in the United States.
2. **Speak directly** with a trained emergency operator through the device’s built-in two-way
speaker.
3. **Help is dispatched** to your GPS location based on your personalized Emergency Care Plan,
including calls to family, neighbors, or emergency services.

If you cannot respond after a fall or button press, our operators use GPS to locate you and follow
your care plan automatically. They dispatch help and begin contacting your emergency contacts
immediately.

## Optional Caregiver App (+$10/mo)

For families who want extra visibility, the Mobile X offers an optional caregiver app for an
additional $10 per month. The app gives authorized family members and caregivers:
* Real-time GPS location of the device
* Device status at a glance without needing to call

For adult children managing a parent’s safety from across the Bay Area or across the country, the
caregiver app provides peace of mind between visits and phone calls.

## Why Bay Area Families Choose Vital Link

Vital Link has served the Northern California community since 1981. We are a family-owned company
based in Oakland, not a national chain shipping boxes from a warehouse. Even though the Mobile X
works anywhere in the United States, every device is set up in person by a local technician who
makes sure you are comfortable before leaving.

We work closely with [hospitals, discharge planners, and case managers][71] throughout Alameda,
Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Napa, Solano, Sonoma, and Santa Cruz
counties. If your loved one is transitioning home after a hospital stay, we coordinate directly with
their care team to ensure protection is in place before they walk through the door.

All equipment is covered by a lifetime replacement warranty at no extra cost. We also ship
replacement charging cradles for free. If something breaks, we fix it.

This GPS medical alert with fall detection is the best fit if you:
* Have experienced a fall or are at higher risk of falling
* Want automatic fall detection that works both at home and on the go
* Want GPS tracking so emergency responders can find you quickly
* Leave the house regularly for errands, walks, appointments, or social activities
* Want a professional to set up the device and train you in person

Also consider our [Mobile W][72] if you prefer fall detection in a wristwatch form factor. Or

### 3. 24/7 Protection

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does fall detection work?

The Mobile X uses built-in sensors to detect sudden changes in motion and impact consistent with a
fall. If a fall is detected, the device automatically contacts our monitoring center. You do not
need to press the button.

### What if the device detects a fall that did not happen?

If the device triggers a false alert, simply tell the operator you are fine. There is no penalty.
The sensors are tuned to minimize false alerts while still detecting real falls.

### Does the Mobile X work outside the Bay Area?

Yes. The device works anywhere in the United States with cellular coverage. Many clients take it
when traveling or visiting family in other states.

### How often do I need to charge it?

The battery lasts up to 5 days on a single charge. Simply place the device in the included charging
cradle when the battery gets low. Low-battery alerts are sent to you and your responder list via
email and text automatically.

### Can I wear it in the shower?

The Mobile X is water resistant and shower-ready. It should not be fully submerged in water such as
in a bath or pool.

### What happens if I press the button but cannot speak?

Our operators use GPS to locate you and follow your Emergency Care Plan automatically. They dispatch
help and begin calling your emergency contacts.

### Who can use the caregiver app?

The caregiver app is an optional add-on for $10 per month. Any family member or caregiver you
authorize can access the app for real-time GPS location and device status.

### Do I need a phone line or internet?

No. The Mobile X uses its own built-in LTE cellular connection. It does not require a landline,
internet, or Wi-Fi.

### What if the device breaks?

All equipment is covered by a lifetime replacement warranty at no cost to you.

### Mission & Vision

[Bay Area Vital Link][68] is a trusted leader in the medical alert systems industry, serving seniors
and families across California with reliable, locally supported solutions. Our mission is to help
older adults and individuals with disabilities live safely, confidently, and independently in their
own homes.

We believe peace of mind comes from dependable technology paired with real human support. That is
why Bay Area Vital Link focuses on high-quality medical alert systems, responsive emergency
monitoring, and personalized service delivered by a dedicated local team.

Our vision is to set the standard for compassionate care in the medical alert industry by treating
every client, family member, and partner with honesty, dignity, and respect. We are committed to
long-term relationships built on trust, transparency, and service excellence.

#### Core Values

## What We Stand For

#### Commitment to You

As a Bay Area medical alert company, we are fair, honest, respectful, courteous, compassionate, and
professional in every interaction. Our commitment to seniors and families comes first in everything
we do.

#### Building Community

As a locally owned Bay Area medical alert provider, we do what we say we will do. We actively
support the communities we serve and build long term relationships with seniors, caregivers, and
local partners.

#### Integrity

Integrity guides every decision we make as a trusted Bay Area medical alert company. We hold
ourselves to the highest standards while contributing positively to the communities we serve.

#### Bay Area Vital Link Link proudly supports community based senior programs across the Bay Area,
#### including Meals on Wheels of Alameda County. Supporting local senior services is part of our
#### long standing commitment to aging safely and independently at home.

[][69]
[Why Us?][70]

### Letter from CEO

It wasn’t long after I started Vital Link Medical Alert Systems back in 1981 that I began to
understand how we made a difference in people’s lives and how working with our clients began to
affect mine.

Back then, I assembled the equipment, handled the sales, installations, administration and made sure
that all our clients were comfortable with using Vital Link.

In the early days I was notified by our monitoring center on every emergency. Many times I would
receive multiple calls throughout the night to make sure that everything went as planned. As we
grew, I couldn’t do that for everyone, but I wanted to keep that personal touch alive. We are still
one of the few medical alert companies that does in home installations and checks up on our clients
to see how they’re after they have used our service.

#### [Read More][71]

Since I took part in all aspects of our business from the start, I’ve always felt very connected to
our clients and felt quite strongly how important Vital Link was to helping them keep their
independence while providing peace of mind to them and their families.

Since 1981, I’ve listened and learned from our clients’ stories and the reasons why they needed our
service. Many have told me how they had fallen and weren’t able to get help as they laid on the
floor all night. My heart went out to them, and I was honored to be able to present a solution to
keep them living safely and independently in their homes.

I always wanted to create a business that took care of people and focused on service and making a
positive impact on our community rather than concentrating on growth and profits. We have always
made a priority of supporting compassionate causes rather than spending resources on marketing and
advertising. We reduce our rates for low income clients, Meals on Wheels recipients and veterans as
a way to give back to those in need. Being President of the Board for Meals on Wheels of Alameda
County allowed me to serve many of our frail, homebound seniors on a volunteer basis. I started
providing pro bono service for our local Holocaust survivors after some of them shared their stories
with my son’s middle school class. I wanted to show him the importance of giving back to our
community and for him to hear the survivor’s experiences while we brought our systems into their
homes.

As a true family business, it’s very rewarding being able to work side by side with my son Asher who
grew up in our business and is now our Director of Operations. Over the years my wife, daughter,
sister, niece and close friends have been and are involved in our company.

In the early days I was able to provide Vital Link services and protect my grandparents and their
peers, then my parents and their friends and now my contemporaries. Even I relied on our service
when both of my hips were replaced and I had limited mobility.

Our goal is to make the entire process courteous, professional and seamless for our clients and
their families. We are here to provide solutions while communicating in a warm and personal way.
When you call us, you will always speak to one of our caring staff directly. There’s no pushing one
for this department or two for that department. Openness, honesty, integrity and respect are at our
core.

You can always be assured that we are going to treat you and yours like family and do exactly what
we say we are going to do. We work hard to go beyond and exceed our client’s expectations. We’re
here to make your life easier and provide you with security and peace of mind.

On behalf of our hardworking staff, I’d like to thank you for the trust you have placed in Vital
Link Medical Alert Systems.

Sincerely,

Arthur Hoffman,

CEO and Founder
Vital Link Medical Alert Systems

all_classified.polished_summary: Vital Link is a family-owned company dedicated to enhancing the safety and independence of seniors in the Bay Area through reliable medical alert systems. Their product lineup includes a range of solutions such as landline and cellular medical alert systems, mobile alerts with GPS, and a modern medical alert watch, all designed to provide 24/7 monitoring and peace of mind for seniors and individuals with disabilities. With a focus on personalized in-home setup and support, Vital Link ensures that its customers remain connected and secure.

# Empowering Independent Living with Remote Health Monitoring Solutions

80% of older adults have at least one chronic condition, and 77% have two or more. With Vitalis
health monitoring, you can track vital signs like blood pressure, oxygen levels, glucose, and heart
rate from the comfort of your home. Get our home healthcare remote monitor and stay connected, safe,
and in control.

## How We Are Making A Difference

Just celebrated my 88 th birthday with a new lease on life. Vitalis has helped me with a weight loss
program and I have lost 25 pounds in three months. The new watch he has available does a great job
of helping me keep track of my vital signs as I continue to lose weight. My husband and daughter
appreciate that the watch also notifies them if I should accidentally fall.
Carmona A.
The blood pressure monitoring has helped me stay on track with taking my meds and I believe is
helping to prevent having another small stroke. It notifies my doctor when my pressure is too high.
Gloria B.
The senior smart watch made it easy to find my mom when she decided to go for a long walk and got
lost and didn’t have her phone. I was able to communicate with her over the watch and geo-locate her
to go get her.

## FAQs

What health conditions can Vitalis devices help monitor?

Vitalis devices monitor vital signs relevant to chronic conditions like hypertension, diabetes,
heart disease, and respiratory issues. Our tools offer real-time insights into blood pressure,
oxygen levels, glucose, and heart rate.

How does the SOS button work during emergencies?
The SOS button on your Vitalis wearable sends an instant alert to your designated emergency contacts
or caregiver through our mobile app. GPS tracking is also activated for rapid location sharing.
Is Vitalis compatible with smartphones and apps?
Yes! All Vitalis devices sync with our easy-to-use mobile app, available on both iOS and Android.
Can I use Vitalis if I’m still active and independent?
Absolutely. Vitalis is built for active seniors who want peace of mind while maintaining
independence.
Is there help available for setting up my device?
Yes, we offer full support! You can contact us for step-by-step setup assistance via phone or email,
and our team will walk you through installation, usage, and troubleshooting.

The device can detect or trigger SOS button press, possible fall, low battery, geo-fence exit, or
abnormal location status.

### Alert Transmission

Alerts can be sent to a mobile app, cloud platform, caregiver, family contact, or monitoring center.

### Caregiver or Platform Response

Care teams or connected platforms can review the alert, check location information, and take action.

lost, or in an emergency situation.

patterns, including sudden movement, impact, and inactivity after the event.

events, or wandering situations.

### Geo-fencing Alerts

supporting elderly care and anti-wandering scenarios.

Our hardware products mainly include smartwatches, sports bracelets, and other sports data
monitoring devices, etc., while our software field focuses on sports data management and health
monitoring software development, thus providing integrated hardware and software solutions.

Since its inception in 2018, we have always been oriented to user needs, and adhere to the
development route of independent research and development, independent manufacturing and independent
marketing.

[WellCare][22] adheres to the values of “honesty, altruism, diligence, and pursuit of excellence”,
striving to achieve a win-win situation with customers, employees, and suppliers. Its mission is to
provide users with cost-effective products. It aspires to become a technology-driven and global
enterprise. The company’s headquarters is located in Shenzhen, China, and it has a manufacturing
center there. Its products are applied in 50+ countries and regions around the world. In recent
years, its performance has consistently maintained a growth rate of over 50%.

## Wizer. Adjective. Having or showing experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

You’ve worked hard, you’ve had many experiences and challenges, and you’ve gained a lot of knowledge
and experience along the way. The later years of your life can be full of adventure, joy, and
excitement. They can also be challenging, with new experiences and life events that will keep you on
your toes. You might find yourself retiring in a new location. Or helping out with the grandkids
while your kids go to work. You might decide to start a new work venture, or to keep investing time
in the career you’ve built. Or, you might decide to travel the world, take up a new hobby, or just
relax and enjoy your free time.

You might be encountering some extra challenges along the way – you might be dealing with reduced
mobility, or learning to deal with your finances in retirement, or having to make some adjustments
to your home as you get older. You may be facing some unexpected health challenges, which usually
come with a hefty price tag. Or, you may feel overwhelmed in the face of having to make some big
life decisions.

Here at Wizerlist, we want to help you navigate this time of your life, taking away some of the
confusion around some of the issues you might face so that you can concentrate on what you really
want to do, and the people you love.

## Our Aims

You might find yourself having to make some big purchases at this stage of your life. From
wheelchairs to medical alert systems, there are a lot of things that you might need to consider.
Technology is advancing, making us more comfortable and secure – but it can be hard to cut through
the marketing speak to know how a product really works and if it’s going to be useful to you. That’s
where we come in – we’ll review products that you might be interested in, helping you to decide if
it’s right before you invest in it.

We also offer guides, like the best states to retire in, or how to find a good retirement community.
We’ll give you a rundown of everything you need to know, so when you’re making a big life decision,
you’ll know what factors to consider.

## What Will You Get from Us?

Here’s how we’ll give you this information:

### Reviews

We’re proud of our reviews – we go in-depth, giving you our honest opinions on a product, breaking
down their features and pros and cons, so that you know whether it’s worth spending your money.
We’ll also explain all the technical details, so that you know if you’re getting a good product or
not – even if you’re not that into technology.

Here are a few examples of our product reviews:
* [Greatcall Touch 3 Review][54]
* [The Life Alert Review – How Does it Work?][55]
* [The Jitterbug Smartphone Review – Is This Simplified Smartphone Right for You?][56]
* [Inogen Gen3 Review – Features, Pros and Cons!][57]

### Product Comparisons

We also directly compare products to help you find the best one. If you’re torn between two
different models of something – like a smartphone – we can help you to decide which one suits your
lifestyle the best. We compare their pricing, features, and pros and cons.

Here are a few of our favourite product comparisons:
* [Life Alert vs Lifeline – Which is the Best Option?][58]
* [Inogen Gen 3 vs Gen 4 – Which is the Best Portable Oxygen Concentrator?][59]
* [Medical Care Alert vs Medical Guardian – Which is Best for You?][60]
* [Consumer Cellular vs Jitterbug – Which is Better?][61]

### Guides

We’re proud of our guides – we do all the research for you, so you can find everything you need to
know in one place. Whether it’s a guide on retirement communities, the best hospital beds, or how to
find the best wheelchair, we’ll cover it in detail, showing you everything you need to look for, as
well as the best products out there on the market.

Here are some of our best guides:
* [How to Make Shoes Non-Slip – Get More Grip!][62]
* [Top 7 Best Orthopedic Seat Cushions to Achieve Pain Relief][63]
* [The Best Chair Lifts for Stairs – Find the Right One for You!][64]
* [The Best Walkers for Seniors – All You Need to Know!][65]

## Our Values

We have some core aims we want to stick to at Wizerlist:

### Promoting Good Value for Money

We know that you will want to spend your money wisely. Aging can bring a lot of monetary challenges,
especially if you suffer from ill-health. That’s why we want to promote products that are affordable
for everyone. If you have a lot of money to spend, you might be tempted to spend it on the latest
and most expensive technology out there – but sometimes, there are more budget-friendly versions of
the same product that can free up some of your money to spend elsewhere.

## Being Informative

We want to give you all the information you need in an easy-to-understand way. We won’t patronize
you – we’ll just give you the facts without any unnecessary embellishments. If you find new
technology overwhelming, don’t worry – we’ll explain what each term means. We’ll break down whether
a product will be useful or not, hopefully saving you wasting your money on time on something that
you don’t need.

### Staying Honest

## Wizer. Adjective. Having or showing experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

You’ve worked hard, you’ve had many experiences and challenges, and you’ve gained a lot of knowledge
and experience along the way. The later years of your life can be full of adventure, joy, and
excitement. They can also be challenging, with new experiences and life events that will keep you on
your toes. You might find yourself retiring in a new location. Or helping out with the grandkids
while your kids go to work. You might decide to start a new work venture, or to keep investing time
in the career you’ve built. Or, you might decide to travel the world, take up a new hobby, or just
relax and enjoy your free time.

You might be encountering some extra challenges along the way – you might be dealing with reduced
mobility, or learning to deal with your finances in retirement, or having to make some adjustments
to your home as you get older. You may be facing some unexpected health challenges, which usually
come with a hefty price tag. Or, you may feel overwhelmed in the face of having to make some big
life decisions.

Here at Wizerlist, we want to help you navigate this time of your life, taking away some of the
confusion around some of the issues you might face so that you can concentrate on what you really
want to do, and the people you love.

## Our Aims

You might find yourself having to make some big purchases at this stage of your life. From
wheelchairs to medical alert systems, there are a lot of things that you might need to consider.
Technology is advancing, making us more comfortable and secure – but it can be hard to cut through
the marketing speak to know how a product really works and if it’s going to be useful to you. That’s
where we come in – we’ll review products that you might be interested in, helping you to decide if
it’s right before you invest in it.

We also offer guides, like the best states to retire in, or how to find a good retirement community.
We’ll give you a rundown of everything you need to know, so when you’re making a big life decision,
you’ll know what factors to consider.

## What Will You Get from Us?

Here’s how we’ll give you this information:

### Reviews

We’re proud of our reviews – we go in-depth, giving you our honest opinions on a product, breaking
down their features and pros and cons, so that you know whether it’s worth spending your money.
We’ll also explain all the technical details, so that you know if you’re getting a good product or
not – even if you’re not that into technology.

Here are a few examples of our product reviews:
* [Greatcall Touch 3 Review][54]
* [The Life Alert Review – How Does it Work?][55]
* [The Jitterbug Smartphone Review – Is This Simplified Smartphone Right for You?][56]
* [Inogen Gen3 Review – Features, Pros and Cons!][57]

### Product Comparisons

We also directly compare products to help you find the best one. If you’re torn between two
different models of something – like a smartphone – we can help you to decide which one suits your
lifestyle the best. We compare their pricing, features, and pros and cons.

Here are a few of our favourite product comparisons:
* [Life Alert vs Lifeline – Which is the Best Option?][58]
* [Inogen Gen 3 vs Gen 4 – Which is the Best Portable Oxygen Concentrator?][59]
* [Medical Care Alert vs Medical Guardian – Which is Best for You?][60]
* [Consumer Cellular vs Jitterbug – Which is Better?][61]

### Guides

We’re proud of our guides – we do all the research for you, so you can find everything you need to
know in one place. Whether it’s a guide on retirement communities, the best hospital beds, or how to
find the best wheelchair, we’ll cover it in detail, showing you everything you need to look for, as
well as the best products out there on the market.

Here are some of our best guides:
* [How to Make Shoes Non-Slip – Get More Grip!][62]
* [Top 7 Best Orthopedic Seat Cushions to Achieve Pain Relief][63]
* [The Best Chair Lifts for Stairs – Find the Right One for You!][64]
* [The Best Walkers for Seniors – All You Need to Know!][65]

## Our Values

We have some core aims we want to stick to at Wizerlist:

### Promoting Good Value for Money

We know that you will want to spend your money wisely. Aging can bring a lot of monetary challenges,
especially if you suffer from ill-health. That’s why we want to promote products that are affordable
for everyone. If you have a lot of money to spend, you might be tempted to spend it on the latest
and most expensive technology out there – but sometimes, there are more budget-friendly versions of
the same product that can free up some of your money to spend elsewhere.

## Being Informative

We want to give you all the information you need in an easy-to-understand way. We won’t patronize
you – we’ll just give you the facts without any unnecessary embellishments. If you find new
technology overwhelming, don’t worry – we’ll explain what each term means. We’ll break down whether
a product will be useful or not, hopefully saving you wasting your money on time on something that
you don’t need.

### Staying Honest

We’ll give you our honest opinions on a product – whether we like it or not! If we like a product,
we’ll give you all the details, letting you know why we think it’s so great. If we don’t like a
product, we’ll highlight the pitfalls, so you don’t have to buy something that doesn’t work as it
should. There are so many products out there on the market aimed at seniors – our honest reviews and
comparisons will help you to find the best ones for you.

## Meet the Team

We have a lot of contributors here at Wizerlist. Our writers are all passionate about the same thing
– giving you all the information you need to have a happy, peaceful retirement. Here’s a bit more
information about our contributors:

## OUR TEAM

A diverse team of talented writers with first hand knowledge of support 55+ family members.

[Alexandra Gavrilescu_-3][Alexandra Gavrilescu_-3]

### Alexandra Gavrilescu

Alexandra Gavrilescu has taken care of both of her grandparents on her mom's side as well as her
grandpa and has a lot of experience that can help others in the same situations. She enjoys giving
advice on Wizerlist to help others.

**Why are you giving advice on Wizerlist?**

I have experience in living and taking care of seniors because I have taken care of both my
grandparents from my mother's side. I took care of my grandpa till he died at the age of 82. It was
hard but I felt it was my duty. Now, with the support and help of my mother, I'm also taking care of
my grandma. She's only 75, but she needs our attention and care 24/7 because of some health issues
and because of her high anxiety level.

Therefore, I know many useful things about caring for seniors and I want to help others find the
right methods to do the same without forgetting about themselves. You must first take care of
yourself to be able to care for others.

**What personal experience do you have with senior living?**

As I said, I took care of my grandpa. I took him to his many doctor appointments, purchased his
meds, and finally, in his last year with us, we had to put him in a retirement home because he
suffered from dementia and he needed assisted care and specialized and professional services. I paid
for all his bills which wasn't an easy period at all. We went to visit him often but once the
pandemic hit, the place was under lockdown, and we could only see him online, on a webcam. After a
couple of months, the people there announced to us that he got infected and developed some serious
lung infection. So, they transferred him to the hospital. We went there but he couldn't make it and
he passed away soon after that. It was terrible even though he was old.

Together with my mom, I'm currently caring for my grandma who's 75 years old. She suffers from
several health conditions, including her kidney infection and urinary tract infection. She's also
extremely anxious so she cannot live on her own. But, we don't want to and cannot afford to put her
in a home, especially since she's ok mentally, despite her high anxiety. So, I'm helping my mother
to take care of her as much as I can. It's quite hard and complicated and it gets me down at times
to see how harsh old age is with people.

**If you could give people one piece of advice about living as a senior, what would it be?**

Patience and empathy are key when it comes to dealing with seniors. As they grow older, their
behavior becomes similar to the ones children have. Obviously, in the most fortunate cases, some
seniors are totally fine and they can take care of themselves, but, the majority of older
individuals need special care and attention. Also, try not to argue with them or contradict them too
much because they already have their habits well-imprinted and they cannot be changed now. Finally,
you should check their meds and make sure they take them, communicate with them, take them out for
walks, and, if you can afford it and you feel overwhelmed, you should also hire help.

[John Hughes_][John Hughes_]

### John Hughes

John Hughes thinks about the future a lot and has a lot of information to share with people. While
he might not be a senior yet, he knows it is coming and wants to prepare. Everything he learns, he
shares with the readers of Wizer List.

**Why are you giving advice on Wizer List?**

We might be young now, but old age is inevitable and it comes with its fair share of challenges.
People experience old age differently, with some maintaining good health, proper finances, and
thriving lives but it is not always this way. However, navigating through this phase of life is much
better for the people and those around them if they have the information needed to improve their
lives. This is what motivates me to give advice on Wizerlist as I try to empower seniors and those
approaching this stage of life to understand what it takes to lead a comfortable life.

**What personal experience do you have with senior living?**

I've grown up with different seniors in my life, and coincidentally they were at extreme ends of the
scale. One was thriving while another was not doing very well. As such, this stark contrast was so
bare and evident that it prompted me to find out why this was the case yet both of them seemed to
lead illustrious lives while they were younger. My little quest made me find out that while they
both had the world at their hands while they were younger, a few simple decisions like the best
retirement plans, where to retire among others are what led to this massive rift between their
lives.

all_classified.polished_summary: ZOLEO Inc. specializes in satellite communication solutions, offering a range of products including the ZOLEO Satellite Communicator and a mobile app designed for seamless messaging in remote areas. Targeting outdoor enthusiasts, businesses, and emergency services, ZOLEO provides reliable connectivity and safety features, ensuring users can stay connected even in the most challenging environments.
